The current expectation is that the threat will remain too limited spatially to warrant a watch issuance

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Thunderstorms are increasing in coverage and intensity this afternoon over the Sangre de Cristo and the Sacramento Mountains within a moist, mid-level flow regime rotating around the upper high. Latest objective analysis suggests that some degree of capping exists across the adjacent High Plains of eastern NM, likely limiting storms to the immediate vicinity of the mountains in the near term, where isolated occurrences of large hail appear possible. Continued daytime heating and resultant air mass destabilization should allow storms to move off the high terrain by late afternoon into this evening with some CAM guidance suggesting an increase in sporadic wind gusts up to 65-75 mph. Current thinking is that the threat will remain somewhat isolated; however, if observational data begin to suggest otherwise, a severe thunderstorm watch may need to be considered

details.label: Summary
details.text: An initially isolated severe storm threat is expected to develop by mid to late afternoon, mainly in the form of large hail up to two inches. The potential for severe wind gusts up to 65-75 mph may increase this evening. A watch is possible by 21-22Z

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Visible satellite and lightning data indicate deepening cumulus and early thunderstorm development from the Laramie Mountains to the Sangre de Cristo Range, as well as along a subtle boundary over east-central CO into northwest KS. The presence of steep low/mid-level lapse rates, surface dewpoints in the 50 to low 60s, and considerable daytime heating are contributing to a destabilizing air mass east of the mountains with MLCAPE expected to increase to 1500-2000 J/kg later this afternoon with minimal convective inhibition. As such, expect storms to gradually move off the high terrain with greater uncertainty in the evolving convection over east-central CO. The presence of 30-35 kt of deep-layer shear may support a few supercells capable of large hail up to two inches as the initial hazard. By this evening, there is some model signal for storms to merge into clusters, at which point the threat for severe winds with gusts up to 65-75 mph would increase
